types.definition: A single principle, standard, or rule used to make a judgment or decision.
types.name: criterion

types.definition: An order relation that formalizes the notion of sorting elements.
types.name: order

types.definition: a contextual circumstance or environmental feature that limits or qualifies the constrained component
types.name: condition

types.definition: indicates the physical, chemical or qualitative condition, including phases, of the constrained component
types.name: state

types.definition: specifies the degree of quality or purity of a substance or generally of the component
types.name: purity

types.definition: an evaluation, assessment, or classification of something against a standardized scale or set of criteria.
types.name: rating

types.definition: refers to the visible, structural, or material state of an object or substance, describing its physical appearance, state of matter, or spatial shape
types.name: physical form

types.definition: the systematic process of facilitating learning, acquiring knowledge, skills, values, beliefs, and habits through instruction, training, research, or discussion.
types.name: education

types.definition: refers to the distinct physiological, kinematic, or mechanical mode of self-propelled movement exhibited by an organism
types.name: locomotion state

types.definition: a significant connection, association, or involvement between two or more people, groups, or entities, characterized by mutual interaction, influence, or relevance.
types.name: relationship

types.definition: an entity—either human, artificial, biological, or organizational—that senses its environment and acts upon it autonomously to achieve a specific goal or purpose.
types.name: agent

types.definition: indicates the cause that explains why the constrained component occurs or holds
types.name: cause

types.definition: specifies the source, provenance, or starting point of the constrained component
types.name: source

types.definition: provides a material type information about the constrained component
types.name: material type

types.definition: indicates the role a person might have in the context of the variable
types.name: role

types.definition: systematic arrangement in groups or categories according to established criteria
types.name: classification

types.definition: provides a location-specific information about the constrained component
types.name: location

types.definition: provides a reference point or information for the constrained component
types.name: reference

types.definition: constraints the component specifying in which layer the variable is measured
types.name: layer

types.definition: indicates the spatial coverage within which the constrained component applies
types.name: spatial extent

types.definition: defines the domain or criteria over which a statistical measure is calculated
types.name: spatial distribution

types.definition: specifies a structural, anatomical, or biological sub-component (e.g., leaf, liver, root, surface layer) of an entity.
types.name: part

types.definition: specifies the spatial orientation, vector heading, or flow orientation (e.g., downward, northward, incoming, outward) of the observed phenomenon relative to a spatial coordinate system, physical boundary, or reference feature.
types.name: direction

types.definition: specifies an area of land or space that shares unifying characteristics, setting it apart from surrounding areas
types.name: region

types.definition: the surrounding area, neighborhood, or general proximity near a specific place or landmark.
types.name: vicinity

types.definition: provides the sampling frequency that applies for the constrained component
types.name: sampling frequency

types.definition: indicates the temporal coverage within which the constrained component applies
types.name: temporal extent

types.definition: provides time-specific information about the constrained component
types.name: time

types.definition: defines how often a final data point is reported
types.name: reporting frequency

types.definition: refers to a process that occurs when measuring the property
types.name: process

types.definition: identifies a specific occurrence, process, or life-stage event (e.g., birth, flooding, surgical procedure) that bounds or triggers the observation, serving as a contextual anchor when explicit calendar time or duration is unknown or non-applicable.
types.name: event

types.definition: restricts the human subject or population to a defined age interval, specific age value, or life stage.
types.name: age

types.definition: a series of systematic, ordered actions or steps taken to achieve a specific end or result.
types.name: process

types.definition: a linguistic mechanism, point of origin, or benchmark used to locate events, actions, or states in time relative to another point in time.
types.name: temporal reference

types.definition: specifies the quantity in which the entity occurs
types.name: quantity

types.definition: provides the range of allowed values
types.name: range

types.definition: defines the value limit that triggers a quality flag, indicating whether the measurement satisfies the threshold criterion.
types.name: threshold

types.definition: specifies the reference quantity to which a measurement is rescaled.
types.name: normalization

types.definition: the distance in the line of advance of a wave from any one point to the next point of corresponding phase
types.name: wavelength

types.definition: the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance, determining how hot or cold it is.
types.name: temperature

types.definition: the length of a straight line through the center of an object or space
types.name: diameter

types.definition: an intrinsic physical property of a material that measures how strongly it opposes or resists the flow of electric current.
types.name: resistivity
